variants.cost: One exact F initialization. Each iteration has two evaluations of Fξ at a common sample and two prox evaluations, plus vector arithmetic and random sampling. Each snapshot refresh needed for a later iteration costs one exact F evaluation. The paper charges p full F evaluations per iteration in expectation; with full F cost N stochastic-evaluation units, N+(2+pN)K is the charged convention including a possible terminal refresh, and an upper accounting bound if that unused terminal evaluation is skipped. Charge 2K prox evaluations separately; the stochastic-oracle count is not an arithmetic or prox-cost bound.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.6 Algorithm 1; pp.8–9 output and tuning; p.9 Remark 5; p.17 Remark 10
variants.name: Algorithm 1, Euclidean setup
variants.output: Return z^K=K^{-1}Σ_{k=0}^{K-1}yk, the half-step average used by Theorem 4. This feasible average is distinct from the last full iterate zK and the snapshot wK.
public_inputs: Exact F and prox_{τg}; stochastic oracle distribution Q with same-sample evaluation at two points.
Deterministic z0=w0∈dom g, L>0, p∈(0,1], γ∈(0,1), iteration count K>=1.
variants.query_and_update: For k=0,...,K-1 set bk=αzk+(1-α)wk and yk=prox_{τg}(bk-τF(wk)). Draw ξk from Q. Evaluate Fξk(yk) and Fξk(wk); set vk=F(wk)+Fξk(yk)-Fξk(wk), zk+1=prox_{τg}(bk-τvk). Set wk+1=zk+1 with probability p and wk+1=wk otherwise. Recompute/cache F at a refreshed snapshot if another iteration needs it; otherwise reuse the cache.
variants.requirements: Finite-dimensional Euclidean geometry; g proper convex lower semicontinuous with exact prox; F monotone with nonempty VI solution set. E Fξ(z)=F(z) and E||Fξ(u)-Fξ(v)||²<=L²||u-v||² on query points. Fresh index draws from Q; the same index must be reused at both queried points. Snapshot refresh is a conditional Bernoulli(p) choice after computing zk+1.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store zk,wk and cached F(wk). Initialize z0=w0∈dom g and evaluate F(w0). For the selected tuning set α=1-p, τ=γ√p/L. The feasible initialization makes every operator query well-defined on dom g.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Run a fixed public K iterations. Theorem 4 tuning is α=1-p, τ=γ√p/L; its displayed constant uses γ=1/2. Corollary 6 proposes p=2/N, which respects p<=1 only when N>=2. Appendix Remark 10 recommends γ=0.99 for practice, distinct from the displayed γ=1/2 constant. No accuracy-based stopping guarantee is certified in this Algorithm record.
